title: [CQ-R10c] Host job frame and verified guest job termination
description:
Objective: the host bridge session sends CQ-R10b's job frame, and the host can prove with fixed probes that no moe-agent process is left in the owned guest. This is R08's handoff item 2: a local kill of `multipass exec` is not evidence that the guest job ended.

Split from CQ-R10 (task-e6411b76f42a43c5b679c725947336af) on 2026-10-29. R10 final consumes this contract.

Contract:
- guest-bridge.mjs exports:
  - AGENT_JOBS: cli -> its allowed credential names. It mirrors guest-supervisor.py JOBS, and a drift test pins the equality.
  - jobFrame({cli, role, credential}): returns the exact CQ-R10b frame bytes through encodeFrame: {kind:'job', version:1, cli, role, credential:{name, value}}, exact keys, value 1-4096 chars of [\x21-\x7e]. A refusal uses a fixed BRIDGE_* code and never echoes the credential.
- guest-session.mjs runGuestSession:
  - gains a required job: {cli, credential:{name, value}}; the role comes from the frozen binding;
  - writes the job frame as the FIRST bytes on the provider's stdin, right after spawn and before any response, bounded by timeoutMs like every other write;
  - refuses invalid job input before spawn with SESSION_INPUT_INVALID.
  The credential never appears in argv, spawn options or env, an error, onOutput, or any other provider call. Existing H1-H5 call sites get the new input and nothing else. No assertion is weakened.
- guest-session.mjs exports endAgentJobs(name, provider = {}, {rounds = 3, sleep, delayMs}), which resolves a frozen {verified: boolean}.
  - It uses lifecycle.mjs invoker() (bounded execFile, shell:false).
  - Each round runs `exec --no-map-working-directory <name> -- sudo -n pkill -KILL -U moe-agent`, then `exec --no-map-working-directory <name> -- sudo -n pgrep -U moe-agent`.
  - verified is true only when pgrep exits exactly 1 (no process left). Exit 0 retries after delayMs. Any other code, provider error or timeout, or running out of rounds, gives verified false.
  - The argv are fixed constants (JOB_IDENTITIES[0]). No other user, process or provider command is touched. It never claims termination it did not observe.

Scope: scripts/local-runner/guest-bridge.mjs, scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs and scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs. Out of scope: the guest supervisor, ledger or lease handling, CLI installation, and any verified-local or isolation claim. Target at most 400 changed lines by git diff --numstat; no size exception exists.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs (on WSL: env -i with the nvm Node 24 PATH).
definitionOfDone: In every session the job frame is byte-exact and is the first write on stdin. Invalid job input refuses before spawn without echoing the credential. The credential is absent from argv, spawn options, errors and output. All shown by tests.

An end-to-end test runs the real supervisor through R10b's main() with injected paths and identity. The job starts with exactly the frame's credential and role in its environment, and a scoped get_context still carries only the host sessionId.

Tests with an injected run show endAgentJobs issuing only the fixed argv. It reports verified only on pgrep exit 1 and retries a still-present process. Any other code, a provider error or running out of rounds reports unverified.
The verification command exits 0, and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
guest-bridge.mjs: AGENT_JOBS and jobFrame, plus tests B16 and B17 (DoD 1).

Base. CQ-R10b (task-7f928d96) must have landed first (dependency). Read its landed guest-supervisor.py: JOBS, read_job, start_job, main(**seams). If its QA changed the contract in task-3b70b824's comment-1630161d, follow the landed code and record the deviation in your step note. Before editing, run step 4's command once for a green baseline.

scripts/local-runner/guest-bridge.mjs:
- `export const AGENT_JOBS = Object.freeze({ claude: Object.freeze(['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', 'CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN']), codex: Object.freeze(['OPENAI_API_KEY', 'CODEX_API_KEY']) })`, with a comment naming guest-supervisor.py JOBS as its mirror.
- `export function jobFrame(job)`:
  - job is a record with exact keys {cli, role, credential};
  - typeof cli === 'string' && Object.hasOwn(AGENT_JOBS, cli), so prototype keys such as 'constructor' are refused;
  - role is 'worker' or 'qa';
  - credential is a record with exact keys {name, value}, AGENT_JOBS[cli].includes(name), and value matches /^[\x21-\x7e]{1,4096}$/.
  - It returns encodeFrame({kind: 'job', version: 1, cli, role, credential: {name, value}}), built from those named fields only, in that key order, under the default MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES.
  - Error handling: any refusal throws bridgeError('BRIDGE_INPUT_INVALID'), whose fixed text never echoes the credential.
- Change exactKeys to compare the own enumerable key set: `const own = Object.keys(value); return own.length === keys.length && own.every(key => keys.includes(key));`. The count-plus-hasOwn form lets a non-enumerable required key stand in for an enumerable extra (Serena gotcha-strict-decoder-key-set).
  - This is one line, and it also hardens validBinding.
  - Inputs that are JSON or object literals behave exactly as before, so every B row stays green.

Tests, in a new CQ-R10c section at the end of scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs. Give the module a credential constant containing 'secret' (e.g. 'sk-secret-R10c!~'), so the existing rejectsWith check, /[\\/]|secret/, catches any echo.
- B16:
  - AGENT_JOBS and both inner arrays are frozen.
  - A codex/qa frame whose value is '!' + 4094 'x' + '~' (exactly 4096 characters) deep-equals framed(JSON.stringify({kind:'job', version:1, cli, role, credential})), byte for byte.
  - Each of these is refused with BRIDGE_INPUT_INVALID, and its message lacks the credential:
    - null, [], an extra key, a missing credential;
    - cli 'gemini' or 'constructor'; role 'architect';
    - credential 'x'; a credential with an extra key; one with a non-enumerable name plus an enumerable extra;
    - OPENAI_API_KEY for claude;
    - values '', 'a b', 'a\x7f', 'café', 4097 characters and 7.
- B17 (skip: NO_GUEST): harness('print(json.dumps({cli: list(names) for cli, (_, names) in m.JOBS.items()}))') deep-equals AGENT_JOBS. It is the drift pin.
implementationPlan.note:
Baseline 4-file gate before editing: exit 0, 296 tests, 295 pass, 1 pre-existing skip (peer work raised the count from R10b's 290).

guest-bridge.mjs (+23/-1): frozen AGENT_JOBS; jobFrame(job) with exact keys {cli, role, credential} and {name, value}, Object.hasOwn on cli, role worker|qa, the name in AGENT_JOBS[cli], value /^[\x21-\x7e]{1,4096}$/. It returns encodeFrame({kind:'job', version:1, cli, role, credential:{name, value}}), built from fields each read once. The whole check sits in a try, so a throwing getter or proxy trap is also BRIDGE_INPUT_INVALID with fixed text. That hardening goes slightly past the plan; B16 has a row for it. exactKeys now compares the own enumerable key set.

The R10b section already defines a local `jobFrame` (encodeFrame for arbitrary values) plus JOB and SECRET, so the import is `jobFrame as hostJobFrame`. That avoids a forward reference to the end of the file. The removed line is the import only. B1-B17 all pass.

implementationPlan.description:
guest-session.mjs: runGuestSession sends the job frame first (DoD 1, DoD 2), plus H-harness compatibility and tests H6 and H7.

scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs, in runGuestSession's validation try block:
- Destructure a required `job`.
- After the binding check, require isRecord(job) with exactly the keys {cli, credential}. A job.role is refused: the role comes only from the frozen binding.
- Compute `first = jobFrame({ cli: job.cli, role: frozen.role, credential: job.credential })` before spawn. This encodes it once, so a later caller edit cannot change it. Keep it on options.
- Error handling: any throw there yields SESSION_INPUT_INVALID through the existing catch, before daemonRefusal, spawn or any provider call.

In relay(), after every listener is attached, issue the first stdin write:
`bounded(session, new Promise((done, failed) => child.stdin.write(options.first, error => (error ? failed(error) : done())))).catch(error => stop(session, error === TIMEOUT ? 'SESSION_TIMEOUT' : 'SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED'))`.
- Node keeps write order, and pump writes only after a request, so the frame is always the first stdin bytes.
- The real supervisor sends hello only after reading it.

Document it:
- runGuestSession's JSDoc: the job input, the first write, and that the credential reaches only that frame, never argv, spawn options, env, an error or output;
- the file header: "its stdin starts with the CQ-R10b job frame".
The argv, spawn options and env stay exactly as today.

Keep the existing tests unchanged:
- fakeProvider: the FIRST stdin write lands in proc.job, through a new optional `first` hook (default: `(chunk, done) => done()`). Every later write goes to proc.written and the existing `write` hook, exactly as now. Every existing written, replies() and exchange() assertion then stays byte-identical, and H4's write hooks still meet the replies they target.
- openSession passes `job: JOB` before `...options`, with JOB a frozen claude/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY job. Call sites get the new input and nothing else.
- H5: supervised()'s harness calls `m.read_job(0, m.JOBS)` before `m.relay(...)`. Otherwise relay() parses the job frame as a host response and exits 76. That one line also proves the host's frame passes the guest's own validator.
No existing assertion changes or weakens. Check that the diff's removed lines are only the import, fakeProvider, openSession and supervised() lines.

Tests:
- H6:
  - For BINDING plus JOB, and for a qa binding plus codex/CODEX_API_KEY: proc.job deep-equals jobFrame({cli, role: binding.role, credential}), the one reply comes after it, and JSON.stringify of [proc.calls, run.outputs, run.forwarded, result] lacks the credential.
  - A `first` hook that never calls done gives SESSION_TIMEOUT, and one that calls done(new Error(credential)) gives SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED. Both run with timeoutMs 100, and HELLO is sent first, so only the job write's own bound is left. Both leave forwarded and written empty, and rejectsWith also proves the message lacks the credential.
  - Invalid jobs refuse with SESSION_INPUT_INVALID and zero provider calls: undefined, null, {cli} alone, a job with role, a claude credential under codex, and the value 'a b'.
- H7 (DoD 2; skip: NO_GUEST; timeout: 30_000), end to end through R10b's main().
  - A supervised-style spawn records launches, makes a temp dir holding the socket and a workspace, and runs:
    `python3 -I -B -c LOAD + code`, where code writes a 0700 probe `#!<sys.executable> -I` with the socket path baked in (argv is the executable alone).
    It then calls `m.main(['bridge'], geteuid=lambda: 0, workspace, sessions, identity=(os.getuid(), os.getgid(), None), jobs={cli: (probe, names) for cli, (_, names) in m.JOBS.items()}, agent_socket=<socket>`, plus `peer_uid=lambda sock: os.getuid()` off Linux, as PEER does). Push the host onto `sessions` so after() cleans up.
  - The probe sends one get_context and reads its answer. It prints JSON with MOE_ROLE, the credential names present in its env, the sha256 of each value (never the value, so onOutput never carries it) and the answer.
  - Run with a qa binding and codex/CODEX_API_KEY. Assert:
    - the result is {observation: EXIT, executionReady: false};
    - the printed role is 'qa', the names are exactly ['CODEX_API_KEY'], and the sha is sha256(credential);
    - the answer is the scoped success;
    - forwarded is exactly [['moe.get_context', {taskId: 'task-abc', workerId: 'worker-1', sessionId: SESSION_ID}]];
    - the launches and outputs lack the credential.
implementationPlan.note:
guest-session.mjs:
- runGuestSession destructures a required `job`. Its own enumerable keys must be exactly {cli, credential}, so a job.role is refused.
- `first = jobFrame({cli: job.cli, role: frozen.role, credential: job.credential})` is encoded once, inside the validation try and before daemonRefusal or spawn. Any throw there gives SESSION_INPUT_INVALID.
- relay() issues the first stdin write after every listener is attached, inside bounded(). A TIMEOUT gives SESSION_TIMEOUT and any other failure SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED.
- The file header and the JSDoc document the job input and the credential's only path. argv, spawn options and env are unchanged.

Harness, with no assertion changed:
- fakeProvider gets an optional `first` hook. The first write lands in proc.job; later writes go to proc.written and `write`, as before.
- openSession passes `job: HOST_JOB` before `...options`.
- supervised() runs `m.read_job(0, m.JOBS)` before relay.
- The removed lines are the import, fakeProvider, openSession and supervised() only, plus one blank line that git's diff re-aligns around the KEY/HOST_JOB insertion.

New tests:
- H6: the first write is byte-exact for worker/claude and qa/codex. A caller mutation after the call has no effect; calls deep-equal [SPAWNED]; the reply follows the frame; the credential is absent from calls, outputs, forwarded and the result. A hung first write gives SESSION_TIMEOUT and done(Error(KEY)) gives SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED, both after HELLO with timeoutMs 100 and with nothing forwarded or written. Six invalid jobs give SESSION_INPUT_INVALID with zero spawn calls.
- H7: end to end through m.main(['bridge'], geteuid=lambda: 0, workspace, sessions, identity=(uid, gid, None), jobs=probe, agent_socket, plus PEER). The probe reports role 'qa', exactly ['CODEX_API_KEY'] beyond the fixed env, sha256(KEY) and the scoped get_context answer.

One deviation from the plan text: H7's forwarded identity is workerId 'qa-1', because the QA binding's workerId is 'qa-1'. The plan's 'worker-1' was a slip; the binding is the authority.

H1-H7 all pass (H4 takes about 1 s, the same as baseline). No orphaned processes and no __pycache__.

guest-session.mjs, endAgentJobs(name, provider = {}, options = {}):
- Imports delay, JOB_IDENTITIES, invoker and QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS. guest-bridge already imports lifecycle and bootstrap, so there is no new cycle.
- Fixed PKILL `sudo -n pkill -KILL -U moe-agent` and PGREP `sudo -n pgrep -c -U moe-agent`, run as `exec --no-map-working-directory <name> -- ...`.
- remote() is async with try/await, so a synchronous throw from run, a non-record resolution, or a timeout/ENOENT/maxBuffer is a transport failure (null). An integer error.code without killed is the remote exit (the runGuestProbe rule).
- Each round sleeps before every round but the first, then runs pkill (any remote exit is accepted; a transport failure ends with false), then pgrep. Exit 1 with /^0\r?\n$/ gives verified true. Exit 0 goes to the next round. Anything else is false at once, and running out of rounds is false.
- Input checks: invoker's throw, options null, rounds outside safe integers 1..10, a non-function sleep, or delayMs outside safe integers 0..60000 each reject SESSION_INPUT_INVALID before any run call.
- It always resolves a frozen {verified}; a rejecting sleep is caught and fails closed.
- The pgrep -c refinement follows the architect's plan and QA note (comment-9cfd6506).

H8 has 15 scripted rows, each [results, verified]. Every result is consumed, so the args must alternate exactly pkill/pgrep, one call per result.
- Verified true: pgrep 0\n, 0\r\n, a pkill exit 255 followed by pgrep 0\n, and a retry after exit 0.
- Verified false: exit 0 three times; exit 1 with '' (the sudo case); '0\n\n'; ' 0\n'; exit 2; a killed timeout; a synchronous throw; ENOENT on pgrep; pkill ENOENT, timeout or throw (no pgrep call).
- Every call is checked for 'multipass', shell false, timeout QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS and killSignal SIGKILL; sleep gets delayMs 7 between rounds.
- One more row checks the default sleep waits for real (rounds 2, delayMs 50, 4 calls).
- 13 invalid-input rows give SESSION_INPUT_INVALID with no run call.

B16/B17 and H1-H8 pass (10/10). Size so far: bridge +23/-1, session +63/-4, tests +172/-9, 272 changed lines in total (cap 400).

I ran the 4-file gate fresh with env -i and the nvm node v24.21.0 PATH: exit 0, 301 tests, 300 pass, 0 fail, 1 pre-existing skip. The baseline was 296/295/1, and the 5 new tests are B16, B17, H6, H7 and H8.
- Size by git diff --numstat: 272 changed lines (+258/-14). That is bridge +23/-1, session +63/-4 and tests +172/-9, under the 400 cap.
- There is no scripts/local-runner/__pycache__, and `pgrep -af 'time[.]sleep[(]600'` finds nothing.
- All three files are LF only, with 0 CR bytes.
- I left the peers' dirty paths alone: source-export.mjs, local-runner.test.mjs, admission.mjs, plus the .moe and root debris.

Adversarial self-review of this task's three files only.

Fixes found by the review, both test-only:
- B16 gains an 'x\n' credential row, for the newline attacker.
- H6 gains a row where stdin.write throws synchronously while the guest then sends a clean HELLO/EXIT/exit 0; it must give SESSION_PROVIDER_FAILED with no observation. Without it, the mutant that ignores a non-timeout job-write error survived, because the stdin 'error' listener masks stream errors.

Mutation sweep in scratch `git archive HEAD scripts` copies plus my 3 files. Each mutant was run under `timeout 120` with `^(B1[67]|H[1-8]) ` and scored by exit code; leftovers were killed by a per-run env marker. The driver and mutant lists are in /tmp/r10c-mut-tools. Result: 31 of 33 mutants killed, and the 2 survivors are equivalent.
- H8 kills: no `-c`, no stdout check, no CR, an unanchored count regex, no retry on 0, retrying after a pgrep or pkill transport failure, an ignored pkill transport failure, killed counted as a remote exit, sleep before round 1, a dropped --no-map-working-directory, and an unchecked rounds, delayMs or sleep.
- H6 kills: frame after the reply (H3/H4 too), no frame, an unbounded first write (30 s timeout), a write error ignored or reported as a timeout, role from job, and unchecked job keys.
- B16 kills: count+hasOwn exactKeys, an unanchored value regex, no 4096 cap, an unchecked name, any role, no try, and unfrozen AGENT_JOBS.
- Other kills: version 2 (B16, H5, H7) and AGENT_JOBS drift (B17).
- Equivalent survivors:
  - `cli in AGENT_JOBS` instead of hasOwn: 'constructor' then reaches AGENT_JOBS.constructor.includes, a TypeError the try/catch turns into BRIDGE_INPUT_INVALID. Only Object.prototype pollution could tell them apart, so the hasOwn is defence in depth. The try/catch is my addition beyond the plan, and this masking is its cost.
  - A missing-job default of ['cli', 'credential']: job.cli then throws a TypeError, giving SESSION_INPUT_INVALID.

Checks:
- The job frame is the first write on the only spawn path. It is issued synchronously after the listeners attach; pump writes only after a request event.
- The credential reaches only options.first. H6 checks calls, outputs, forwarded and the result; H7 checks launches and all output bytes.
- verified is true only for pgrep exit 1 with a '0' count.
- No B1-B15, S, I, J or H1-H5 assertion changed.
- executionReady and verified-local are untouched. There are no .moe edits and no Git writes.

Residuals for R10 final:
- The job itself holds its credential and may print it; its output reaches onOutput unfiltered, by design.
- endAgentJobs kills every moe-agent process in the VM, so the caller must hold R06's per-VM job lease.
- The worst case is 3 rounds × 2 calls × 30 s plus delays, about 182 s.
- A guest root that lies about pgrep is out of scope.

Final fresh gate: exit 0, 301 tests, 300 pass, 1 pre-existing skip. Windows node v24.16 on the bridge file: 55 tests, 22 pass, 0 fail, 33 NO_GUEST skips (B16, H6 and H8 pass). Size 280 (+266/-14). LF only, no __pycache__, no orphans.

comments.author: architect-bd1eb82d
comments.content:
The CQ-R10b guest contract this task builds on (R10b plan rev 1; planned, not landed). If R10b's QA changes any of it, follow the landed code.

Job table:
- `JOBS[cli] = (executable, credential names)`, with `claude` mapping to `/opt/moe/agents/claude` and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, and `codex` mapping to `/opt/moe/agents/codex` and OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY.
- AGENT_JOBS's drift test can read `{cli: list(names) for cli, (_, names) in m.JOBS.items()}`.

Test seams for the end-to-end DoD 2 (Python keywords only):
- `main(argv, geteuid=os.geteuid, **seams)` forwards the seams to `start_job(in_fd, out_fd, workspace, sessions, identity=(uid, gid, groups|None), jobs, agent_socket, peer_uid)`.
- A non-root test passes `identity=(os.getuid(), os.getgid(), None)`, because setgroups needs root.
- It needs a temp `agent_socket` for get_context.
- Pass `peer_uid` off Linux, as H5's PEER does.
- relay() treats stdin EOF as a gone host, so keep the bridge's stdin open while the job runs.

Frame and exit codes:
- The frame is read byte-exact before hello. Every later stdin byte belongs to relay().
- Refusals write no frame: 65 for a bad frame, 74 for EOF before the frame, 66 for no workspace, and 71 for no account or session home.
- The job env is exactly: PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, HOME (a fresh home under /var/lib/moe/sessions), USER and LOGNAME both moe-agent, LANG=C.UTF-8, MOE_ROLE, and the one credential variable.

comments.author: architect-bd1eb82d
comments.content:
Architect note for QA (plan rev 1). The plan deliberately departs from the description's literal PGREP argv.

The description says `sudo -n pgrep -U moe-agent`, verified on exit 1. The plan uses `sudo -n pgrep -c -U moe-agent` instead, and verified needs exit 1 AND stdout matching /^0\r?\n$/.

Why: exit 1 alone is ambiguous.
- `sudo -n` exits 1 on its own failures. Checked on this box, it prints "sudo: a password is required" and leaves stdout empty.
- Multipass's CommandLineError is 1 as well.
- Only `pgrep -c` prints a count, and it prints exactly `0` when nothing matched (procps-ng 4.0.4, the Ubuntu 24.04 version).

So the literal check could claim a termination nobody observed. The refined one keeps DoD 3 ("verified only on pgrep exit 1"). The optional CR allows for a Windows host's Multipass.

R10 final's step 1 is amended to the same argv and fake answers (amend-1).

Also, for QA, a test-harness change that leaves every pre-existing H assertion byte-identical: fakeProvider records its first stdin write as `proc.job`, and H6 pins that write as the job frame.

comments.author: qa-952969be

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Keeping the task's literal `pgrep -U` with an exit-1 test. Rejected: `sudo -n` failures and Multipass's CommandLineError also exit 1 with empty stdout, which would claim a termination never observed. `pgrep -c` plus exactly '0' disambiguates.
2) Updating each H assertion that inspects proc.written or replies() for the new first frame. Rejected: it churns about 12 assertions. The fake provider capturing its first write as proc.job keeps them byte-identical, and H6 pins the first-write property directly.
3) Converting H5 to main(). Rejected: H5's agent needs argv, and main() gives the job argv [executable] only. A one-line m.read_job in its harness keeps H5 and also cross-checks the host frame against the guest validator. H7 covers main() end to end (DoD 2).
4) A local strict key check in jobFrame. Rejected in favour of fixing the shared exactKeys helper (one line). It hardens validBinding too, and no JSON or literal input changes behaviour.
5) Printing the credential from the H7 probe. Rejected: the job's output reaches onOutput. The probe prints its sha256.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Architect prototype (copies in /tmp/claude-1000/r10c-proto/), built on the R10b prototype (/tmp/claude-1000/r10b-proto/), not on landed R10b; rebuild it on what R10b actually lands.
- Size: 201 changed lines (bridge +17/-1, session +34/-3, tests +139/-7).
- The full 4-file gate: 288 tests, 287 pass, 1 pre-existing skip, 0 fail. With the runtime and the three harness tweaks alone, all 50 bridge tests passed.

Codebase facts:
- runGuestProbe (guest-readiness.mjs) already treats an integer error.code without error.killed as the remote exit, with error.stdout.
- invoker(name, provider) validates the name and provider and runs execFile with shell false, killSignal SIGKILL and maxBuffer.
- QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000 is exported by lifecycle.mjs.
- R10b's start_job accepts peer_uid, so H7 runs on macOS too.
- relay() treats stdin EOF as a gone host, and runGuestSession keeps stdin open until teardown.
- rejectsWith already refuses a message containing 'secret' or a path.

R10 final consumes runGuestSession({..., job}) and endAgentJobs(name, provider, {rounds, sleep, delayMs}) -> frozen {verified}.
planningNotes.risks:
- The fake provider's first-write capture must not route the job frame through the existing `write` hook, or H4's hung- and failed-write rows would trip on the job frame instead of their reply.
- Without the read_job line, H5's real supervisor exits 76. Remember that line if R10b renames read_job.
- H7 needs the socket path baked into the probe, because argv is the executable alone. Keep macOS's AF_UNIX path length in mind (H5 already runs there).
- endAgentJobs must stop on a pkill transport failure, never treat it as 'nothing to kill'.
- Zombies that are never reaped exhaust the rounds and report unverified. That fails closed.
- On WSL, run under env -i with the nvm Node 24 PATH. After any mutation sweep, check for orphans with `pgrep -af 'time[.]sleep[(]600'` (mem gotcha-local-runner-supervisor-tests).

verification.outputTail:
✔ X7 end to end, a dirty checkout round-trips through the real supervisor and only the agent changes come back, never a refused one (878.943749ms)
✔ A1 invalid input is refused before any temp dir or Git process: a bare git, a relative repo, a forged candidate (141.031215ms)
✔ A2 a candidate must fit its base: a delete names a base blob, and a file never replaces, covers or sits beneath a non-blob (889.17101ms)
✔ A3 the admitted tree is the base minus deletes plus files, byte for byte, with no autocrlf, eol or ident conversion (637.800952ms)
✔ A4 admission changes no ref, index or worktree byte and runs no candidate file: the active controller stays in place (183.78636ms)
